subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` as the supported explicit escape hatch for early provider recovery, alongside existing automatic cooldown probes?
rationale: The implementation can be reviewed mechanically, but choosing a permanent public CLI recovery contract—and whether shell-only recovery is sufficient—requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Adopt the explicit reset
options.body: Approve the profile-scoped command as an opt-in operator escape hatch after inspectable real behavior proof confirms the complete recovery flow.

options.title: Use guided recovery instead
options.body: Pause this command and implement the action through Doctor or an in-product Fix surface so affected users do not need terminal knowledge.

options.title: Rely on automatic probes
options.body: Close the PR if maintainers want early recovery handled only by runtime probing and fallback policy rather than manual state mutation.

recommendation.title: Adopt the explicit reset
recommendation.body: Approve the profile-scoped command as an opt-in operator escape hatch after inspectable real behavior proof confirms the complete recovery flow.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal combines major auth-profile invariant work with merger responsibility for related cooldown changes.
